run.script_question: Cross-region uniqueness with fully-qualified sequences - do three independent per-region deployments issue colliding raw numbers that only the prefix separates?
run.executed_by: Cortex Code - sequential statements via sql_execute; T7.3 via three concurrent snow CLI sessions coordinated by a barrier table
run.teardown_skip_reason: Teardown intentionally not run, consistent with all previous runs. The script's OWN cleanup block was run at the start, which removed the 06 leftovers.
run.headline: R12 IS PROVEN. The fully-qualified sequence reference fixed what 06 could not do. For the first time across four attempts the sensitivity gate OPENED: the three regions genuinely issued the SAME raw numbers (all 1-500, 1000 collisions), and the prefixed keys were still 30000/30000 unique across three measured-concurrent sessions. T7.4 returned SOUND with 10000 raw values shared by all 3 regions.
notes_on_completeness: query_id and elapsed_ms are null for every statement: no QUERY_HISTORY lookup was performed. No values were inferred or fabricated.

TWO DEVIATIONS from the script as written, both recorded in full below and both forced by Snowflake behaviour rather than chosen: the CREATE FUNCTION ordering at seq 19-23, and a corrected T7.2 verdict at seq 36-45. Neither changes what was tested.

Three statements failed. Two are genuine findings about CREATE-time name resolution (seq 19, 21). The third is the script's own T7.2 verdict returning a false FAIL (seq 35) - explained at finding F24.
Two diagnostics not in the script were added (seq 46, 54) to establish a sound T7.2 baseline and to illustrate the collision concretely.

deviations_from_script.script_as_written: Line 57 sets USE SCHEMA POC_SCHEMA, then lines 79-117 create all seven functions using qualified function names such as W6V7_NA.regional_key_v7.
deviations_from_script.what_happened: Creating W6V7_NA.regional_key_v7 from POC_SCHEMA FAILED: "Object 'LM_POC_DB.POC_SCHEMA.REGION_MAP_V7' does not exist or not authorized." The unqualified TABLE reference region_map_v7 was resolved against the SESSION'S CURRENT SCHEMA at CREATE time, not against the function's own schema. Creating W6V7_NA.raw_key_unqualified_v7 from POC_SCHEMA likewise FAILED with "invalid identifier 'EMP_SEQ_V7.NEXTVAL'".
deviations_from_script.deviation_applied: Each function was created while the session's current schema was set to that function's own schema (USE SCHEMA W6V7_NA / W6V7_EU / W6V7_APAC), which is what script 06 did implicitly.
deviations_from_script.why_this_is_faithful: The script's stated intent at line 65 is that 'the region map stays unqualified, which is the one case the docs get right'. Honouring that requires the function to be created where its map is visible. The function bodies are byte-identical to the script; only the session's current schema at CREATE time differs.
deviations_from_script.evidence_retained: Both failures are recorded verbatim at seq 19 and seq 21 rather than discarded, because they are a genuine refinement of 06's finding F19. See finding F23.

deviations_from_script.script_as_written: Line 180 resets ONLY W6V7_NA's sequence, then the verdict at lines 186-195 flags any non-NA sequence with NEXT_VALUE > 1 as 'FAIL - a foreign sequence advanced'.
deviations_from_script.what_happened: The verdict returned FAIL for both EU and APAC. This is a FALSE FAIL. T7.1 immediately beforehand drew 500 values from each of EU and APAC, legitimately leaving both at 601. Because only NA is reset, the check cannot distinguish leftover state from contamination.
deviations_from_script.deviation_applied: The script's verdict was run and recorded verbatim at seq 35, then a corrected T7.2 was run at seq 36-45: all THREE sequences reset to 1, baseline confirmed, the three cross-schema calls repeated, and a before/after comparison used instead of an absolute threshold.
deviations_from_script.why_this_is_faithful: The script's own note at lines 196-197 states the real criterion: 'what matters is that EU's and APAC's stay at 1'. The corrected test measures exactly that. The property under test is unchanged.
deviations_from_script.evidence_retained: Both the false FAIL and the corrected PASS are recorded. See finding F24.

concurrency_method.how_it_was_achieved: Three independent `snow sql -f` processes, each its own Snowflake session, released together by a barrier table (w6_barrier) polled every 250ms inside a Snowflake Scripting block.
concurrency_method.deliberate_design_choice: All three sessions ran with current schema POC_SCHEMA rather than their own region's schema. That is not a shortcut - it is the T7.2 property being exercised under load: with the sequence fully qualified, the key must not depend on the caller's schema.
concurrency_method.overlap_evidence: T7.3b at seq 50. All three windows overlapped for 1092ms against durations of 1207-1984ms.

statements.purpose: OVERLAP - mandatory. The script supplies no SQL; this query is carried over from the R10 run.
statements.sql:
WITH w AS (
    SELECT TAG, SESSION_ID,
           MAX(CASE WHEN PHASE = 'INSERT_START' THEN TS END) AS t_start,
           MAX(CASE WHEN PHASE = 'INSERT_END'   THEN TS END) AS t_end
    FROM w6_run_log WHERE TAG IN ('V7NA','V7EU','V7AP')
    GROUP BY TAG, SESSION_ID
)
SELECT TAG, SESSION_ID,
       TO_VARCHAR(t_start,'HH24:MI:SS.FF3') AS insert_start_utc,
       TO_VARCHAR(t_end,'HH24:MI:SS.FF3')   AS insert_end_utc,
       DATEDIFF(millisecond, t_start, t_end) AS duration_ms,
       DATEDIFF(millisecond, (SELECT MAX(t_start) FROM w), (SELECT MIN(t_end) FROM w)) AS mutual_overlap_ms,
       CASE WHEN DATEDIFF(millisecond, (SELECT MAX(t_start) FROM w), (SELECT MIN(t_end) FROM w)) > 0
            THEN 'CONCURRENT - all three windows overlap'
            ELSE 'NOT CONCURRENT - windows disjoint' END AS verdict
FROM w ORDER BY TAG
statements.observation: All three started within 115ms of each other and overlapped for 1092ms against durations of 1207-1984ms.

statements.purpose: THE TEST THAT DECIDES R12. Was the prefix actually load-bearing?
statements.sql:
WITH parts AS (
    SELECT REGION, K % 1000000000000000 AS seq_part FROM LM_POC_DB.POC_SCHEMA.w6v7_global_keys
),
shared AS (
    SELECT seq_part, COUNT(DISTINCT REGION) AS region_count FROM parts GROUP BY seq_part
)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM parts)                         AS total_keys,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shared WHERE region_count > 1) AS raw_values_shared,
       (SELECT MAX(region_count) FROM shared)               AS max_regions_per_raw_value,
       CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shared WHERE region_count > 1) = 0
            THEN 'VACUOUS - no raw value reused; the prefix was NOT load-bearing. R12 still unproven.'
            ELSE 'SOUND - raw values WERE reused across regions and the prefixed keys are still unique. R12 PROVEN.'
       END AS verdict
rows: SOUND - raw values WERE reused across regions and the prefixed keys are still unique. R12 PROVEN.
statements.verdict: SOUND - R12 PROVEN. EXACT MATCH TO EXPECTATION
statements.observation: Every one of the 10,000 raw sequence values was issued in ALL THREE regions, and all 30,000 prefixed keys remain unique. Removing the prefix would have produced 20,000 duplicates. The prefix is demonstrably the thing keeping the regions apart - which is precisely what 04's T4.7, 05's T5.2 and 06 all failed to establish.

statements.purpose: DOES EVERY KEY DECODE TO ITS ISSUING REGION? (R13)
statements.sql:
WITH codes AS (
    SELECT 'North America' AS region_name, 1 AS region_code
    UNION ALL SELECT 'EU', 2 UNION ALL SELECT 'APAC', 3
)
SELECT g.REGION, COUNT(*) AS keys_issued,
       SUM(CASE WHEN FLOOR(g.K / 1000000000000000) = c.region_code THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS decode_correct,
       CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = SUM(CASE WHEN FLOOR(g.K / 1000000000000000) = c.region_code THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
            THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS verdict
FROM LM_POC_DB.POC_SCHEMA.w6v7_global_keys g
JOIN codes c ON c.region_name = g.REGION
GROUP BY g.REGION ORDER BY g.REGION

matched_rules: T7.0 CONFIRMED -> the asymmetry is real and pinned as a regression. Build standard: ALWAYS fully qualify sequences inside a UDF body.
T7.1 collides AND T7.4 SOUND AND T7.3 shows 0 duplicates -> R12 PROVEN under the real topology.
T7.2 passes -> the key no longer depends on session state, which is the property that makes this safe to ship.
decision_table_resolution.r13_verdict: PROVEN - reconfirmed under the real colliding topology, which is stronger than the earlier confirmations
decision_table_resolution.r8_verdict: RESOLVED WITH A CONDITION. Identical function text CAN be deployed per region, but ONLY if the sequence is fully qualified. The qualified form means the text is no longer literally identical across regions - each carries its own schema name. Production already does this via orchestrator substitution (Q2 line 50), so the design is consistent with what is deployed today.
build_standard_decisions: ALWAYS fully qualify the SEQUENCE inside a UDF body. An unqualified sequence follows the caller's current schema and will silently draw the wrong one, or fail with invalid identifier.
Create each function while the session's current schema is that function's own schema, so unqualified TABLE references bind locally. Alternatively qualify the table too - see finding F23.
Adopt T7.0 as a standing regression test. It is cheap and catches the asymmetry returning.
Adopt T7.1 and T7.4 as mandatory preconditions for any future cross-region uniqueness claim. Three earlier packs produced vacuous passes without them.

findings.title: Unqualified identifiers in a UDF body are validated at CREATE time against the caller's schema; tables then BIND, sequences RE-RESOLVE at run time
findings.evidence: Seq 19: creating a function in W6V7_NA from POC_SCHEMA failed because the unqualified TABLE region_map_v7 was looked up as LM_POC_DB.POC_SCHEMA.REGION_MAP_V7. Seq 21: the unqualified SEQUENCE emp_seq_v7 likewise failed at CREATE from POC_SCHEMA with invalid identifier. Seq 23 and 24: both succeeded unchanged once the session's current schema was the function's own schema. 06's seq 31-33 had already shown that after creation, a table keeps pointing at the bound object while a sequence follows the caller.
findings.interpretation: A single rule explains all observations. Unqualified names are resolved against the session's current schema at CREATE time, which is why creation fails if they are absent there. Tables are then permanently bound to the object resolved. Sequences are not bound - the identifier is re-resolved on every invocation against whatever the caller's current schema is.
findings.implication: This is a cleaner and more useful statement than 06's F19, which described the post-creation behaviour as 'table resolves to the function's schema'. It only appeared that way because 06 created each function while sitting in its own schema. The practical rule for the build standard is twofold: qualify the sequence always, and create the function in its own schema (or qualify the table too) so the table binds where intended.
findings.status: Open - recommend this supersede F19's wording in the design documentation.

findings.title: T7.2's verdict produces a false FAIL because it resets only one of the three sequences
findings.evidence: Seq 43 resets only W6V7_NA, per script line 180. Seq 45 then flags EU and APAC as 'FAIL - a foreign sequence advanced' on the basis of NEXT_VALUE > 1. Both read 601, which is exactly where T7.1's 500-row draws left them. The corrected test at seq 46-48, with all three reset to 1, shows EU and APAC remaining at 1 while NA advances to 201.
findings.interpretation: The verdict uses an absolute threshold where a before/after comparison is required. It cannot distinguish legitimate leftover state from caller-schema leakage.
findings.implication: Low risk to the conclusion, because the script's own note at lines 196-197 states the correct criterion and the corrected test applies it. But a reader seeing only the script's output would conclude qualification had failed, when the opposite is true. Recommend the script either reset all three sequences before T7.2 or capture a before snapshot and compare.

findings.title: With a fully-qualified sequence, the region prefix is demonstrably load-bearing and cross-region uniqueness holds under concurrency
findings.evidence: T7.1 (seq 41-42): all three regions drew raw values 1-500, giving 1500 rows with only 500 distinct and 1000 collisions. T7.3a (seq 51): 30000 rows, 30000 distinct keys, 0 duplicates, 3 sessions. T7.3b (seq 52): all three insert windows overlapped for 1092ms. T7.4 (seq 53): 10000 raw values each shared by all 3 regions, max_regions_per_raw_value = 3, verdict SOUND. T7.4 illustration (seq 54): raw value 1 became 1000000000000001, 2000000000000001 and 3000000000000001.
findings.interpretation: For the first time the precondition and the postcondition are both satisfied. Without the prefix the 30,000 keys would have contained 20,000 duplicates; with it there are none. The prefix is doing the work, not the sequences.
findings.implication: R12 is closed. R13 is reconfirmed on the same data, and more strongly than before because the earlier confirmations ran without collisions. Taken with R10's result, the design's uniqueness properties now hold under both the shared-sequence and independent-per-region topologies.

findings.title: The _V7 naming and the opening cleanup block worked - 06's F20 trap did not recur
findings.evidence: Seq 1-5 dropped 06's schemas and the two leftover tables before anything was created. Every object in this run carries a _V7 suffix. T7.1 produced the expected collisions on the first attempt rather than plausible-looking numbers from a stranger object.
findings.interpretation: 06's near-miss, where a leftover POC_SCHEMA.W6_EMPLOYEE_SEQ from the R2 run was silently consumed, was prevented by design rather than by luck.
findings.implication: Retain both practices for future packs: an explicit cleanup block at the top, and run-scoped object names. Together they remove the class of error that made 06's failure quiet rather than loud.
